subject: Performance discovery: end-to-end p95/p99 targets + PoC next actions
messages:
From: Anita Desai <anita@novamed.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@novamed.ai>
Date: 2027-06-25T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro / performance goals for end-to-end latency

Rishi, thanks again for the call today — helpful to see Redwood's latency breakdowns. A quick recap from our side and a couple clarifying questions so we can map expectations to our current provider's numbers:

- Goal: p95 <= 200ms end-to-end for text completions (average prompt length ~80 tokens); p99 <= 450ms.
- Current provider (IncumbentAI) observed: p95 ~= 320ms, p99 ~= 900ms (heavy tail during bursts).
- Streaming: we stream partial tokens to front-end; typical concurrency 80–120 simultaneous sessions in us-east.
- Throughput shape: steady-state 12–20 rps, 3x short bursts up to 350 rps for ~45s during peak events.

Questions:
1) Can Redwood demonstrate p95/p99 under a replayed traffic shape (we’ll provide CSV)?
2) Any special headers or trace tokens you need to preserve streaming timing fidelity?
3) What level of KV-cache / prefix-caching assumptions should we use for the PoC?

I’m attaching a traffic_profile.csv and a first-draft slo_test_plan.pdf with our ask. If we can run a 1–2 hour replay on your hosted API with the same model family we use (LlamaX-13B quantized), that’ll be ideal.

Next steps from Novamed: we can provide a masked dataset for replay, a set of API keys limited to the PoC IPs, and a list of representative prompt sizes.

Thanks —
Anita
Head of Product
Novamed

[Attachment: traffic_profile.csv (CSV, 18KB)]
[Attachment: slo_test_plan.pdf (PDF, 280KB)]

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Desai <anita@novamed.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-25T16:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance discovery: end-to-end p95/p99 targets + PoC next actions

Anita — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments, very helpful. High level response and proposed plan below.

High-level feasibility:
- Hosted API: based on your traffic profile and target model family, we believe p95 <= 180ms and p99 <= 400ms is achievable with configuration we propose (streaming enabled, aggressive prefix cache, and 2x burst headroom).
- Where things bite: p99 under 3x burst (350 rps) is where tail amplification happens — we'll need a short controlled replay to validate backpressure handling and fallbacks.

PoC proposal (short):
1) Redwood runs a 2-hour controlled replay against our hosted inference cluster using your replay CSV and masked payloads. We'll mirror headers/timestamps for streaming fidelity.
2) Test profile: steady 15 rps sustained + 3 bursts (45s) that hit 350 rps; concurrency target 100 active streams.
3) Metrics collected: per-token latency, network RTT, time-to-first-subtoken (TTFTS), p50/p95/p99 end-to-end (client->frontend->model->client), error rate and retransmit/backpressure events.
4) Warmed KV cache: we'll run a pre-warm pass to simulate prefix caching; we'll also run a cold-start segment to measure differences.
5) Acceptance gates: p95 <= 200ms and p99 <= 500ms for the majority (>=90%) of steady-state period; explainers for tail events.

We can do the PoC as soon as next week. Can you confirm:
- Which exact model variant you want to test (LlamaX-13B-QLo or LlamaX-13B-8Q)?
- Will you provide sample keys and IP allowlist, or should we issue a temporary PoC token?

I’ll loop Soojin for the replay orchestration and Marissa to own measurement validation and post-test analysis.

Thanks, 
Rishi
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: replay_instructions.md (MD, 6KB)]

From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@novamed.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Anita Desai <anita@novamed.ai>
Cc: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-26T09:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance discovery: end-to-end p95/p99 targets + PoC next actions

Rishi — quick clarifications from infra:

- Model variant: we currently run LlamaX-13B-8Q in production. We can test LlamaX-13B-QLo too if Redwood supports it, but primary ask is 8Q parity.
- Keys/IPs: we can either provide a short-lived key and IP allowlist or give you a set of sample traces to replay from your side. Preference: you run the replay from your infra to avoid egress throttles on our side.
- KV-cache: our prompts include a stable system prompt (~400 tokens) + short user message. So prefix caching should target the first 400 tokens.

Tentative window: Tue 2027-06-29 09:00–11:00 PT. That fits our SRE calendar.

Carlos
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Novamed

From: soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@novamed.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Anita Desai <anita@novamed.ai>
Date: 2027-06-26T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Performance discovery: end-to-end p95/p99 targets + PoC next actions

Carlos / team — perfect, thanks. Operational notes from our side:

- We'll provision a dedicated PoC pool in us-east with the same model family (13B 8-bit path) and enable streaming with identical chunking behavior to reduce client-side differences.
- Replay fidelity: please attach the CSV with millisecond timestamps and include a column for "is_streaming" so we can mirror chunk timing.
- Telemetry: we'll produce a consolidated CSV with per-request p50/p95/p99, and a separate file with token-level timings for the streaming windows.
- Failure modes: if we detect sustained queueing > 200ms at the ingress, we'll automatically trigger a second run with scaled batch size and an alternative quantized kernel to observe tradeoffs.

Action items (owners):
- Novamed: provide final traffic_profile.csv + confirmation that LlamaX-13B-8Q is the canonical variant (owner: Carlos) [Due: 2027-06-27].
- Redwood infra: provision PoC pool + issue temporary PoC API key (owner: Soojin) [Due: 2027-06-28].
- Measurement & analysis: run replay, produce results spreadsheet + tail analysis (owner: Marissa) [Due: 2027-06-30].

I’ll block Tue 2027-06-29 08:30–12:00 PT on our side to run checks and run the replay. If that window shifts, please flag.

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Anita Desai <anita@novamed.ai>, Carlos Mendez <carlos.mendez@novamed.ai>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, soojin_lee <soojin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-06-28T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Final schedule & success criteria for p95/p99 replay (Novamed)

Team — quick post-run checklist and what we’ll deliver after the PoC run on Tue: 2027-06-29

Deliverables (post-run):
- Result set: per-request CSV (timestamps, request id, p50/p95/p99, error flag), aggregated latency histogram, and token-timing slices for streaming traces.
- Tail analysis: root-cause notes for any p99 violations (e.g., queue buildup, model kernel stalls, network spikes).
- Cost snapshot: estimated per-1M tokens served in the tested config and projected savings vs incumbent.
- Rollout recommendation: if acceptance gates pass, a suggested steady-state config (pool size, batching target, cache TTLs) and an A/B plan for incremental traffic shift.

Acceptance criteria reminder (from Rishi’s note):
- p95 <= 200ms for steady-state (>=90% of steady window).
- p99 <= 500ms with documented mitigation for tail bursts.

If we pass, next commercial step is a dedicated-reserved sizing exercise (we'll draft an SOW). If we miss, we’ll capture mitigation actions and a follow-up re-run plan.

See you Tue.
Marissa
Performance & Observability, Redwood Inference
